en: [Beginning of fragment CUL Or. 131.1 fol. 2]—and they were all prophesied by the Blessed One:
"In this very way, Mañjuśrī, after ten *kalpas*, those monks shall attain unexcelled, perfect enlightenment in the *buddha*-field of the Tathāgata Duṣprasaha during the *kalpa* called Vimalaprabhāsa.
They shall become Tathāgatas of a single name, named Praṇidhānālaṃkāravyūharāja."

In this way, Mañjuśrī, the hearing of this Dharma-discourse by Bodhisattvas is [superior]. And, Mañjuśrī, if one were to practice the six perfections for a thousand eons while endowed with skill in means, yet another, having written down this Dharma-discourse and possessing faith, were to recite it even once after the passing of half a month—the former mass of merit would not approach even a hundredth part of this [latter’s merit].

It does not bear comparison even to a thousandth part, nor even a hundred-thousandth part; it does not admit of any calculation, nor any fraction, nor any analogy, nor any resemblance—indeed, it does not even admit of a point of comparison.
Therefore, Mañjuśrī, I entrust this Dharma-discourse to you. In the future time, these Bodhisattvas of mine shall uphold such [teachings], and this Dharma-discourse must be maintained and taught.

Mañjuśrī, it is just as follows: for as long as a universal monarch (cakravartin) remains, his seven treasures do not disappear; but when the universal monarch passes away, those seven treasures disappear. In the very same way, Mañjuśrī, for as long as such sūtras as these circulate in the world, for that long the thirty-seven factors of enlightenment (bodhipākṣikā dharmāḥ) of the Tathāgata will not disappear. But when such sūtras have disappeared, there will be the disappearance of the Buddha-dharma.

Therefore, Mañjuśrī, you should uphold, recite, and teach these very jewels of sūtras of such a kind. Bodhisattvas, mahāsattvas, must not be those who have failed to initiate vigor; this is our instruction, lest you later fall into regret.

Thus spoke the Blessed One; and the Bodhisattva Sumati, the youthful Mañjuśrī, those Bodhisattvas, those monks, and that entire world—including its gods, humans, asuras, and gandharvas—rejoiced in what the Blessed One had said.
The *Sumatidārikāparipṛcchā-nāma-mahāyāna-sūtra* is completed. May there be auspiciousness! [+++]
